problems.form_value: direction treatment_higher, which the form says 'follows the p. 15 sentence'; statistics_available [regression_coefficient_se, p_value_only, figure_only], so the p. 15 'β = 0.20, p = .04' is credited to this pair
problems.source_says: The table the form cites does not show a significant difference for this pair. Table A2 gives Control -0.162 (SE 0.090) relative to Low-Agency with no star, and one star marks p < .05. No Table A2 coefficient equals 0.20 (usefulness: High-Agency -0.026, Control -0.162, both relative to Low-Agency), so the p. 15 'β = 0.20' matches no printed model. That sentence also names no comparison group, so crediting it to the control arm is an inference, which form-spec rule 1 forbids. The abstract (p. 2) and the Discussion (p. 17) both say usefulness did not differ. Fix: code direction no_clear_difference, drop p_value_only from this pair, and keep the p. 15 sentence in 'reported' as an unexplained conflict. The form flags the conflict itself (agreed_fields_checked, confirmed: false) but keeps the value that the source does not support. Eligibility is unaffected.
problems.quote: First, at the individual level we observed no significant differences in the ideas as assessed by third-party evaluators’ subjective ratings of overall creativity, originality, and usefulness.
problems.locator: p. 17, Discussion; p. 2, Abstract; p. 35, Table A2 (Usefulness column and star note); p. 15, Results, Individual-Level Creativity

problems.where: S1-O5, S1-O6, and S1-O7, contrast Low-Agency vs Control (ai_vs_bau)
problems.source_says: Each permutation test prints its statistic as well as its p-value: the observed difference between the maximum and minimum condition means, 3.33 clusters (p = .04), 0.22 in noise ratio (p = .02), and 0.75 in coefficient of variation (p = .005). More than a p-value is printed, so test_statistic fits better than p_value_only. The numbers in 'reported' are correct. This is minor and changes no direction, construct, unit, or eligibility decision.
problems.quote: we conducted permutation tests (n = 5,000 permutations) comparing the maximum and minimum condition means for each metric. For the number of unique clusters, the observed difference between conditions was 3.33

confirmed: Criterion 3 holds. S1-O1 to S1-O3 are third-party ratings of the submitted ideas, not self-reports: 'Next, we asked our evaluators to rate the compliant ideas from the submitters', and the models predict 'creativity, originality and usefulness ratings from third-party evaluators' (p. 13, Evaluation Phase; p. 15, Results).

S1-O4 to S1-O7 are computed on the submitted ideas: cosine similarity of all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embeddings (384 dimensions) to a leave-one-out condition-object centroid, and HDBSCAN cluster metrics on sentence embeddings (p. 14, Analytic Approach; p. 15, Homogeneity; pp. 16-17; p. 32, Figure 3).

AI was available while every analyzed AI-arm idea was written. AI-arm participants 'entered their alternative uses below the web-app interface', and 'Object trials from the high- and low-agency conditions were excluded if they did not include chat data'. The control had no web-app. Everything took place in one session, so timing is immediate and no outcome is after_ai (p. 12, Occasions; p. 13, Manipulation Checks).
The question codes follow the codebook rule: with_ai for the three rated constructs and across_people for the four diversity measures, all produced with AI available (codebook section 1).

The constructs fit the Table A1 rubric. Overall creativity is the rater's 'single, overall impression', originality 'means an idea is new, uncommon, or unique' (novelty), and usefulness 'means the idea is effective, appropriate, or valuable in some way' (p. 34, Table A1).

Diversity in S1-O4 to S1-O7 compares different people's ideas. Each sampled idea is compared with 'the average embedding of all ideas other than the one being compared' in its condition and object, and clusters were formed 'for each combination of object and condition'. No outcome measures variety within one person's ideas (p. 15; p. 32, Figure 3 note).

The measure codes fit. CloudResearch Connect adults are lay crowd raters (human_raters). Centroid similarity is embedding_similarity. Cluster count, noise share, and cluster-size CV come from clustering (category_count) (p. 10, Participants; p. 15; p. 17).

Unit rating for S1-O1 to S1-O3 has support. The models predict 'ratings from third-party evaluators', and Table A2's 1,709 rows exceed the 1,685 ideas in Table A3's 337 compliant participant-object trials (337 x 5), which fits one row per rating, not one per idea. The paper never defines a row in words (p. 15; p. 35, Table A2; p. 36, Table A3).

Unit output with n_units 337 for S1-O4: 'for each participant we randomly sampled one idea they had generated for each object', and Table A3 has Num.Obs. 337. Unit set for S1-O5 to S1-O7: the metrics are computed per condition-object pool and the tests compare 'the maximum and minimum condition means' (p. 15; p. 36, Table A3; p. 17).

Table A2 matches the form exactly: Creativity 2.537*** (0.103), High-Agency -0.040 (0.091), Control -0.082 (0.081); Originality 2.514*** (0.136), -0.010 (0.110), -0.077 (0.098); Usefulness 2.955*** (0.087), -0.026 (0.101), -0.162 (0.090); Num.Obs. 1709 in each model; Low-Agency is the reference level (p. 35, Table A2).

Table A3 and p. 16 match the form: Intercept 0.441*** (0.015), High-Agency -0.050* (0.021), Control -0.014 (0.019), Num.Obs. 337; F(2, 121.67) = 3.15, p < .05, partial eta squared .07; Tukey t(125) = -2.45, p < .05 (high vs low agency) and t(122) = 1.87, p = .15 (high agency vs control) (p. 36, Table A3; p. 16).

The cluster settings and permutation results match: minimum cluster size 6, minimum samples 1, epsilon 0.25, 5,000 permutations, and differences 3.33 (p = .04), 0.22 (p = .02), and 0.75 (p = .005), each driven by control vs low agency (p. 17).

The directions on the diversity scale are right. High-agency ideas were 'less similar to the condition-object centroid' than low-agency ideas, so treatment_higher. Fewer clusters, a lower noise ratio, and a higher CV in the low-agency arm all mean less diversity, because 'a higher CV suggests greater imbalance in cluster sizes' and noise marks outlier ideas 'indicative of greater diversity' (p. 16; p. 17).

Coding the centroid score as similarity is right despite the p. 15 formula '1 - cosine'. Table A3's column is 'Cosine Similarity to Centroid', Figure 2's axis is cosine similarity, and p. 16 reads 'indicated by greater cosine similarity scores in the low-agency condition' (p. 15; p. 16; p. 31, Figure 2; p. 36, Table A3).

The primary status holds. H1 (creativity, originality, usefulness) and H2 (homogeneity) are the preregistered hypotheses, models were fit 'for each of the preregistered outcome metrics', and the cluster analysis is 'an exploratory clustering analysis' (p. 9; p. 15; p. 16; p. 2, Abstract).

No outcome that bears on the three questions is missing. Participant-AI similarity compares only the two AI arms on overlap with the AI's suggestions (ps > .05). Submitter self-ratings and perceived uniqueness are self-reports. Every submitter gave exactly five ideas per object (n = 2,250), so there is no fluency outcome. Prompt types and chat behavior are process measures (p. 37; p. 12; p. 14; pp. 38-42).

S1-O1 and S1-O2 directions no_clear_difference hold, and the form records the printed 'ps > .60' correctly. Note for extraction: Table A2's Low-Agency vs Control coefficients (-0.082 with SE 0.081, -0.077 with SE 0.098) are about one standard error from zero, which cannot give p > .60, so the printed bound fits only the high-agency vs control pair. The form flags this only indirectly in open_questions (p. 15; p. 35, Table A2).

The Discussion says the low-agency CV was 'significantly greater' than both other conditions, but no low vs high agency test is printed. The form keeps this claim in the S1-O7 notes rather than coding a contrast, which fits rule 8 (p. 18; p. 17).
summary: The core coding of c132 holds: evaluator ratings (S1-O1 to S1-O3) and embedding and cluster measures (S1-O4 to S1-O7) are scored on ideas written with the chatbot available, the question, construct, measure, and unit codes follow the codebook, and every number in 'reported' matches Tables A2 and A3 and pp. 15-17. The conclusion is refuted on one direction code, S1-O3's Low-Agency vs Control 'treatment_higher', which rests on a p. 15 sentence that names no comparison group and cites a β absent from Table A2, while Table A2 (-0.162, SE 0.090, no star), the abstract, and the Discussion show no significant difference (a minor second point: the permutation contrasts print their test statistic, so 'p_value_only' understates them).
